content.text:
All four deliverables are done and committed on `plain/fpga-scope` (4 commits, not pushed). All three configs meet 100 MHz post-route, and the capture buffer maps to block RAM in every one.

## Deliverables

| # | Deliverable | Status |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `fpga/xilinx/scope_axil_top.sv` | **Pass** ΓÇö `s_axi_*` ports, `PROBE_W`/`DEPTH_LOG2` pass through |
| 2 | `build.tcl` + `scope.xdc`, three configs | **Pass** ΓÇö lint, synth, opt/place/route, reports in `fpga/xilinx/reports/<cfg>/` |
| 3 | xsim regression (`sim/run_xsim.ps1`) | **Pass** ΓÇö `tb_smoke`, `tb_csr`, `tb_csr_if` and a new `tb_axil_top` all print `TB_RESULT: PASS` |
| 4 | `fpga/xilinx/README.md` | **Pass** ΓÇö every number traces to a committed report or log |

## Results (xc7a100tcsg324-1, 100 MHz, out-of-context, post-route)

| Config | LUT | FF | RAMB36 | RAMB18 | Buffer bits | WNS | TNS | Capture buffer maps to |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| (32, 8) | 1,194 | 1,182 | 0 | 2 | 8,448 | +0.791 ns | 0 | 1 ├ù RAMB18 |
| (32, 12) | 1,238 | 1,213 | 4 | 1 | 135,168 | +0.603 ns | 0 | 4 ├ù RAMB36 |
| (32, 15) | 1,282 | 1,256 | 33 | 1 | 1,081,344 | +0.906 ns | 0 | 33 ├ù RAMB36 |

- **Distributed RAM:** zero LUTs are used as memory in any config. The one RAMB18 not used by the buffer is the window-metadata RAM.
- **Lint:** 0 errors, 0 critical warnings, 6 warnings, identical across configs. Five are the repo's intentional `unused` sinks and one is a benign explicit truncation; none needs a change.
- **DRC:** one warning (`CFGBVS-1`), a board-level property deliberately not set in an out-of-context module.

## Things you should know

- **I changed `rtl/scope_csr.sv` to close timing.** With the original RTL the (32, 8) build failed 100 MHz (WNS ΓêÆ0.211 ns, 30 failing endpoints). The comparator lane mask was computed from the runtime address; it is now a constant table with the same behaviour. Baseline reports with the original file are in `reports/_baseline/`.
- **`rtl/scope_top.sv` had a use-before-declaration** that xsim rejects outright. I moved four wire declarations up, with no functional change.
- **`tb_csr` does need the Python golden vectors**, contrary to the brief. The xsim script generates them first, so it needs `python` on PATH.
- **xsim 2025.2 mis-simulates the `tb_csr` status-poll loops** (legal SystemVerilog, not a Verilator-only construct). I rewrote the two loops and committed a standalone reproducer, `sim/xsim_repro_loop_cast.sv`. Six other testbenches still use the same idiom and will fail in xsim until edited.
- **IP Integrator rejects a SystemVerilog top as a module reference.** I added a zero-logic Verilog shim, `scope_axil_bd.v`, for block designs; `check_ipi.tcl` confirms `s_axi` is inferred as an AXI4-Lite slave through it.
- **Port hold is excluded in the XDC.** Out of context the clock has no routed net, so every port path shows an artificial hold violation; internal hold is still checked and is positive. Port hold must be closed in the parent design.
- **The reset port is `aresetn` (active low)**, registered once into the core's active-high reset. `RLE_EN` defaults to 1 so buffer bits match the Agilex table.
- **`run_all.ps1` retries one transient Vivado error.** A scratch-directory lock killed three parallel builds late in the session; the reruns gave identical results.

Beyond what you asked, I added `tb_axil_top` to `sim/run.sh` and ran the full Verilator regression under WSL: 17 of 17 pass with `-Wall` (`sim/verilator_run.log`). That run used an LF-normalised copy because the Windows checkout's CRLF endings break `bash`.

## Not done

- The four SymbiYosys formal proofs were not re-run after the RTL edits; `sby` is not installed here.
- No bitstream or hardware run.
- The other 13 testbenches were not ported to xsim.
- Only the three `PROBE_W=32` configs were built; wider probes are untested and may not meet 100 MHz, since margin is under 1 ns.

## Things you should know

- **I changed `rtl/scope_csr.sv` to close timing.** With the original RTL the (32, 8) build failed 100 MHz (WNS ΓêÆ0.211 ns, 30 failing endpoints). The comparator lane mask was computed from the runtime address; it is now a constant table with the same behaviour. Baseline reports with the original file are in `reports/_baseline/`.
- **`rtl/scope_top.sv` had a use-before-declaration** that xsim rejects outright. I moved four wire declarations up, with no functional change.
- **`tb_csr` does need the Python golden vectors**, contrary to the brief. The xsim script generates them first, so it needs `python` on PATH.
- **xsim 2025.2 mis-simulates the `tb_csr` status-poll loops** (legal SystemVerilog, not a Verilator-only construct). I rewrote the two loops and committed a standalone reproducer, `sim/xsim_repro_loop_cast.sv`. Six other testbenches still use the same idiom and will fail in xsim until edited.
- **IP Integrator rejects a SystemVerilog top as a module reference.** I added a zero-logic Verilog shim, `scope_axil_bd.v`, for block designs; `check_ipi.tcl` confirms `s_axi` is inferred as an AXI4-Lite slave through it.
- **Port hold is excluded in the XDC.** Out of context the clock has no routed net, so every port path shows an artificial hold violation; internal hold is still checked and is positive. Port hold must be closed in the parent design.
- **The reset port is `aresetn` (active low)**, registered once into the core's active-high reset. `RLE_EN` defaults to 1 so buffer bits match the Agilex table.
- **`run_all.ps1` retries one transient Vivado error.** A scratch-directory lock killed three parallel builds late in the session; the reruns gave identical results.

Beyond what you asked, I added `tb_axil_top` to `sim/run.sh` and ran the full Verilator regression under WSL: 17 of 17 pass with `-Wall` (`sim/verilator_run.log`). That run used an LF-normalised copy because the Windows checkout's CRLF endings break `bash`.
